title: Ormanetto (nuncio in Spain) to Cardinal of Como, 1573: copy of Philip II's letter with two cipher passages (ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 7; DECODE R116)

documents.shelfmark: ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 7, ff. 303r-304r, address f. 320v (DECODE R116)
documents.route: Madrid (nunciature) -> Rome (Cardinal of Como, Secretariat of State)

plaintext.source: No decifrato found; the clear Spanish frame is not a crib. Reading first made by A. Devadas, 1 Oct 2026.

transcription.source: DECODE DOC_R116_D2580 (KL, 2020), spot-checked against images IMG_R116_I863/I864
transcription.notes: Digits with dots and underlines; the cross-stroke 't' after 2/4/5 is transcribed as a digit 1. The cross-stroke after 2/4/5 (written 1) is the word-end mark; undotted 0 closes the digit before it, dotted 0 opens the next. Five signs corrected from the full-resolution scans on 5 Oct 2026 (r116_cipher_v2.txt): a dotted superscript 7 (col), a stroke-4 without dot, a dotted 0 lost in a paper hole (desidera), and two writer's dot slips (entri, particular).

system.summary: Homophonic substitution on digit signs (two per letter, dotted and undotted, zero rule), a stroke on 2/4/5 as word end, a small nomenclator, no doubled letters, final nulls: the Spain nunciature's 'cifra ordinaria'.
system.sibling_key: none (key reconstructed by A. Devadas from R116 and R118 together; Meister p. 265 prints only the rules)
system.notes: Tested and ruled out: Lasry's 1568 Spain key, Meister's Crivelli 1561 key and his Ottoboniana keys VI.1-VI.3 (Como-era, incl. Spain nomenclator). Meister p. 265 prints the rules of the 'cifra ordinaria di mons. nuntio di Spagna' but not its table.

prior_solution.where: No earlier reading known; the reading is A. Devadas's of 1 Oct 2026, made from this project's published files after the 21 Sept attempt.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded. On 1 Oct 2026 an outside solver (A. Devadas) emailed a key; the owner asked the model to verify it against the project's own transcription and to write it up.
tools: polyanneal.py (polyphonic pair annealer with Viterbi scoring)
dec_aj.py (decoder rebuilt from the emailed key description)
measure.py (token-level sense measure with an attested-word lexicon from lang/ corpora; measure_control.py shuffled-key control)

solution.what: Downloaded the DECODE images, the address leaf and the KL transcription of R116 with the session cookie.
Read the clear frame: a copy of Philip II's letter to the bishop of Padua (Ormanetto); address leaf to the Cardinal of Como, docketed 17 June 1573. DECODE's '7 Jan 1573' is the volume heading.
Ran Lasry's 1568 Spain nunciature polyphonic key (targets/alessandrino1568/decrypt.py).
Simple/homophonic substitution over three sign sets, Spanish and Italian 4-gram annealing.
Solver check on a known text: first quadgram solver failed its own control; replaced by the KL-penalised annealer, which reads a same-length Italian homophonic control.
Dandini-frame structure (2-digit letters with even second digit, 3 digits + mark as codes); pair-parity test per line.
Web and PARES search for a printed edition or the King's minute; Carini 1894 located but not online; PARES has only 1575 Ormanetto items.
Meister 1906, Ottoboniana collection 1573-87: found the Como keys with Spain nomenclator and the rules of the Spain nuncio's ordinary cipher.
Decoded with Meister VI.1 (Como, Spain nomenclator), Crivelli 1561 polyphonic key, and checked VI.2/VI.3 structure.
Polyphonic digit = two letters with unknown pairs, annealed; also with 1 as null and 0 as letter.
Same polyphonic annealer on 1,100 digits of Alessandrino R97 recovers 7 of 9 of Lasry's pairs (-2.18/char); R116 scores worse and restarts disagree.
Pooled R116 with R118 (1,660 signs; 4t = barred 4) and reran the polyphonic annealer.
Academic catalogues for an edition of Ormanetto's nunciature: Fernández Terricabras 2000 (no full text online); no register edition found.
Tomokiyo's cryptiana pages on papal and Spanish ciphers: no Ormanetto item, no decipherment.
Spanish royal-cipher syllabic structure (base digit + dot/mark vowel indicator), annealed in Spanish and Italian.

Outside key: A. Devadas (with Claude) emailed his reconstruction of the Spain nunciature's cifra ordinaria, built from this project's published images and ciphertext files, with a report of the reading of R116 and R118.

Rebuilt the decoder from the key description (dec_aj.py) and applied it to our own r116_cipher.txt: both passages read as Italian (ho visto il foglio mandatomi a parte sopra le cose di Pitigliano ...).
Italian per-letter score of the decode with the 16 well-supported code groups: -3.02 against a best of -6.69 over 200 letter-shuffled keys (mean -8.50).
The same key reads R118 (ormanetto1576), whose leaf carries the contemporary decipherment; the dateline and the 'qua' syllable group agree.
Code values graded by AJ kept as he graded them; the guessed and open groups (about a dozen) were not adopted without a second context.
Fetched the two full-resolution scans (IMG_R116_I863_P1, I864_P2, 2136x3075) with the DECODE session cookie.

Checked how the 0.90 was measured: it was AJ's count of words (112 of 139 non-code words ordinary Italian), code groups left out and nothing measured per token or for sense. Wrote measure.py: every cipher token (digits and word-end strokes) counted, a word read only if its letter runs split into words attested in the it-renaissance + it-nunziature corpora (cipher spelling) or its code value is adopted; on DECODE's unchanged transcription: 1,248/1,324 = 94.3%.

Re-transcribed every unread stretch on the full-resolution scans. f.303r: the 'dol' sign is a struck sign with a dotted 7 written above (col); the 4 before 'si oferisce' is a stroke-4, its dot is not there (che si oferisce); 'oftri' is written 6 0̇ 6 0̇ 7 (a dot slipped one place from 6 0 6̇ 0̇ 7, entri); 'pbrticular' has an undotted 4 (writer's slip for 4̇, particular). f.304r: the sign in 'desi?bera' is a dotted round sign lost in a paper hole, 0̇ by shape, giving 0̇4 = d (desidera, echoed by 'io desidero'). Corrected file r116_cipher_v2.txt.

Open codes pooled across R116 and R118: 32, 2̇88, 84, 42, 53 occur once each in R116 and not at all in R118's reading; 3̇22 is Italia twice (after 47/93 tutta) but stands where 'per' is wanted in 'che sia [3̇22] alterarla'. No second context; left open.

measure.py on r116_cipher_v2.txt: A 739/756, B 559/568, 1,298/1,324 = 98.0% read as sense; strictest variant (single-context codes 62, 48, 4̇22, 47/93, 3̇22 also counted unread) 1,258/1,324 = 95.0%. Shuffled letter keys with the codes kept: mean 23.0%, max 32.9% (measure_control.py).

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The Spain nunciature's cifra ordinaria, reconstructed by A. Devadas from R116 and R118 and emailed on 1 Oct 2026, was applied to this project's transcription of R116 and reads both passages as Italian; checked by a shuffled-key control and by the same key reading R118.

gaps.item: code groups 32 and 2̇88 in 'l'ho [32] de la buona [2̇88] havuta' (f.303r)
gaps.detail: one context each, not in R118, no key sheet; 9 tokens

gaps.item: code groups 84 and 42 in 'sara [84] che S.S.ta [42] dalla parte sua' (f.303r)
gaps.detail: context suggests bene / ancora, but other words fit; counted unread; 8 tokens
3̇22 is Italia twice, 'per' wanted here; 53 reads 'fi' as letters (dittography?) or a code; 9 tokens

outcome.notes: Measured 5 Oct 2026 with measure.py: 1,298 of 1,324 cipher tokens (98.0%) belong to words read as sense, A 97.8%, B 98.4%; strictest variant 95.0%; shuffled-key control 23% mean. Five signs re-read on the scans. The earlier 0.90 was AJ's word estimate (non-code words only), not a token measure. Italian: passage A is Philip II on the league and the Emperor, B on Pitigliano. Pitigliano not checked against 1573 sources.
